name: Palate Archive — BCI Taste Memory Parlor
description: Palate Archive offers curated taste-memory sessions via direct BCI gustatory overlay, allowing clients to experience meals that no longer exist — pre-Collapse cuisine made from ingredients now extinct or economically inaccessible — sourced from donated or purchased memory engrams from elderly donors and high-fidelity culinary archivists. A single session might include the precise sensory experience of a 2041 Oaxacan mole negro, a 2019 Osaka ramen, or a grandmother's specific recipe for jollof rice as remembered in perfect neural fidelity. The parlor also offers emotional-context packages that layer in the ambient memory of the meal's original social setting.
story_hooks: A client undergoing a routine heritage taste session experiences memories that are clearly not from the advertised donor — they're from someone who is still alive, and the memories include witnessing a murder
A Shelf elder realizes her late husband's taste memories are being commercially sold without her knowledge and sets out to have them removed from the catalog by any means necessary

A food archivist discovers that one of the parlor's most popular 'historical' recipes is actually a fabrication — a synthetic memory constructed to match what people wish pre-Collapse food tasted like
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Space Elevator Tether System
